criteria.name: Post-reform violence trajectory
criteria.description: Assess how violence levels changed immediately after the administrative restructuring and whether they rebounded, indicating only temporary relief rather than durable stabilization.

criteria.name: Continuity of legacy conflicts
criteria.description: Examine whether pre-existing ethnic and boundary disputes persisted with similar actors and grievances despite the new regional configurations.

criteria.name: Effectiveness of cluster governance
criteria.description: Evaluate whether smaller administrative units improved representation, service delivery, and conflict management, or reproduced previous governance shortcomings.

criteria.name: Federal intervention patterns
criteria.description: Analyze the frequency and triggers of federal security deployments and whether they provide lasting stability or only short-term containment.

criteria.name: Autonomy demands and repression
criteria.description: Track how authorities respond to renewed or ongoing autonomy requests and whether crackdowns correlate with escalations in unrest.

criteria.name: Localized conflict intensity
criteria.description: Assess the extent to which violence remains geographically localized yet capable of overwhelming local authorities and causing significant displacement.

criteria.name: Civic unrest over service failures
criteria.description: Evaluate protests and strikes related to unpaid salaries and service delivery, and whether these are holdovers from prior administrative issues.

criteria.name: Violence against civilians trend
criteria.description: Monitor the prevalence of attacks targeting civilians and whether such incidents are increasing alongside intercommunal clashes.

criteria.name: Border and intergroup disputes
criteria.description: Identify friction points at administrative boundaries within and between new regions and whether clustering shifted or intensified these disputes.

criteria.name: Elite mobilization and militias
criteria.description: Examine how local elites organize ethnic-based militias to contest territory and resources, and whether incentives changed under the new structure.

criteria.name: Institutional maturity and capacity
criteria.description: Assess the pace at which new regional institutions staff, coordinate, and deliver governance, and whether institutional immaturity fuels insecurity.

criteria.name: Spillover implications nationwide
criteria.description: Consider how outcomes in the former region inform potential national restructuring efforts, including risks of resistance to further administrative changes.

criteria.name: Conflict drivers beyond administration
criteria.description: Distinguish structural factors—identity politics, resource competition, and power struggles—from administrative design to gauge root causes of violence.

criteria.name: Reconciliation efforts’ impact
criteria.description: Evaluate the effectiveness and durability of local peace or reconciliation initiatives and whether they translate into reduced incidents.

criteria.name: Exposure and humanitarian impact
criteria.description: Assess the scale of populations exposed to political violence and related displacement, even when conflicts remain localized.

criteria.name: Security-service tradeoffs
criteria.description: Analyze whether prioritizing security responses coincides with neglect of public services, potentially feeding grievance cycles.

criteria.name: Comparative regional hotspots
criteria.description: Contextualize trends relative to other regions experiencing insurgency and state-insurgent conflict, to see if similar dynamics are at play.

criteria.name: Administrative restructuring limits
criteria.description: Test the assumption that creating smaller units reduces conflict, probing cases where reorganization did not resolve underlying disputes.

criteria.name: Communication and legitimacy
criteria.description: Assess how top-down decision-making affects public buy-in and the perceived legitimacy of new regional authorities.

criteria.name: Escalation triggers and thresholds
criteria.description: Identify events—such as autonomy crackdowns, boundary changes, or militia seizures of towns—that precipitate sharp spikes in violence.
